newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Kokh says Transneft sale will take time.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Kokh says Transneft sale will take time.

text.p: Russia's proposed sale of a state stake in crude oil pipeline monopoly AO Transneft will not take place soon because of potential conflicts of interest that must be worked out, privatisation minister Alfred Kokh said on Thursday.

"I would not hurry to privatise it because it is a unique organisation and we have not yet completely worked out the privatisation plan," Kokh, a deputy prime minister and head of the State Property Fund told a news conference.
He gave no timetable for Transneft's privatisation, but he said that potential conflicts of interest over levying transport tariffs would make privatisation difficult.
Privatisation officials have said they planned to sell a 24 percent stake in Transneft this year.

Kokh said Transneft was one of Russia's four natural monopolies -- major companies with no competitors, including national electric company RAO Unified Energy System, RAO Gazprom natural gas group and the railroads.
